summary.intent: Continue and complete GSD Phase 70.1 (rotation read-plane durability and crash-resume soundness) through wave-based parallel execution, resolve the Wave-7 desktop-e2e (D-16) acceptance checkpoint, then run the full /ship-phase flow (verify/secure/validate/simplify/SDK-E2E/CodeRabbit/ship/resolve reviews) to open and merge a PR.
summary.outcome: All 13 plans executed and merged across 7 waves; D-16 desktop-e2e acceptance passed on macOS/Linux/Windows after fixing a real revocation-bypass bug, a double-publish bug, and a macOS idle-mount publish-queue starvation bug; PR #598 opened, CodeRabbit/Greptile findings triaged (fixed a real TS/Rust parity checkpoint-GC bug plus CI-only gate breaks), all 7 review threads resolved, and CI was being driven to fully green with a final floor_store Windows-cfg fix in flight when the transcript ends.

repo: gsd commit helper can report `commit_failed` as a false negative while the commit actually lands — always verify with `git log`, never blindly retry
cargo fmt -p <crate> reformats the WHOLE crate (not just touched files) and strands out-of-scope drift; must revert unrelated files after formatting
This repo's CI does NOT run `cargo fmt --check` at all, so local `cargo fmt` before commit is unnecessary churn and risks rustfmt-version skew vs already-passing code

Windows CI job builds with `--features winfsp` not `fuse`; test modules using `crate::test_support` must be gated `#[cfg(all(test, feature = "fuse"))]`, not bare `#[cfg(test)]`, or they break on Windows only
Permission-based test fault injection (chmod) only works on Unix; such tests must be `#[cfg(unix)]`-gated or they silently no-op and fail assertions on Windows
The SC#6 grep gate requires a `// sc6-allow:` marker within roughly a ±1-line window directly above a raw IPNS resolve call
A 96-commit branch with no PR hides branch-wide CI gates (SC#6 grep gate, Windows cargo job) until the first real PR-triggered CI run — open PRs earlier to surface these sooner
gh pr edit fails on this repo (Projects-classic GraphQL); patch PR body via `gh api -X PATCH .../pulls/<N> -F body=@file` instead
PR titles/commit subjects must be conventional and paren-free (commitlint + lint-pr-title reject parens in the subject, though `type(scope):` scopes like `(fuse)` are fine)
CodeRabbit CLI bundles findings differently from the PR-level review; CLI run pre-PR + PR-level bot review can both surface real, non-overlapping bugs

rust-analyzer diagnostics (E0063, dead_code, unused-import) are frequently stale mid-edit snapshots during concurrent agent edits — always confirm with an authoritative `cargo check`/`cargo test` before trusting them
Rust rotate_read engine (TS + Rust twin) previously discarded RotateReadResult at the FUSE gate, leaving the in-memory grant-root read key stale — closed via Fix A (refresh_grant_root_read_key)

Covalesced scope-exit delete (root_children_override) reduces grant-root publish count from +2/+3 to exactly +1 by having the engine reseal with a caller-supplied post-delete child list instead of resolving live children

macOS FUSE-T defers file release ~40s and the publish queue is edge-triggered (only drains on a subsequent FUSE op) with no wall-clock backstop — an idle mount can silently starve a queued parent republish indefinitely

TS/Rust rotation engines must be fixed in lockstep — CodeRabbit caught the TS engine GC'ing an ECIES checkpoint before the parent's batched republish committed, while the Rust twin already deferred correctly via pending_checkpoint_node_ids

code.finding: rotate_read_on_scope_exit now takes &mut CipherBoxFS, captures RotateReadResult, and refreshes the grant-root inode's in-memory read_key via refresh_grant_root_read_key (line ~556) to close a revocation-bypass where a subsequent relink resealed the folder under the stale old key

build_scope_exit_child_override originally failed OPEN per-child (continue/warn+skip on missing child or build_child_refs error) and REPLACED the grant-root's published child list, silently dropping/orphaning transiently-unresolvable siblings; fixed to propagate errors and fail closed to EIO, mirroring the fail-closed sibling build_folder_metadata

verify_subtree_clean's is_dirty signal was discarded (only .frontier kept); the Skipped-branch convergence check used frontier.is_empty() alone, which would mis-mark a missing root as converged on resume; fixed by keeping both fields and gating the short-circuit on !is_dirty

repairDirtyNode called deleteWrappedKey immediately after decrementing a multi-child parent's pending count (even when the decrement didn't trigger the parent's republish), risking permanent checkpoint loss on a crash between GC and the batched republish; ported the Rust twin's deferred design via a new pendingCheckpointNodeIds field, flushed only after updateFolderMetadataAndPublish commits

persist_wrapped_key held decoded plaintext key bytes in a plain Vec<u8> (not zeroized) while sibling get_wrapped_key already used Zeroizing; fixed for hygiene. Also owner_private_key field was plain Vec<u8> instead of Zeroizing, fixed to match phase's zeroization discipline

Three independent JsonSidecarFloorStore instances (generation, seq, checkpoint) pointed at the same rotation-high-water.json but each built its own Arc<Mutex<()>>, racing on a shared deterministic .tmp rename path; fixed with a process-global path-keyed shared lock registry (SIDECAR_LOCKS/shared_lock_for)

load_all_for_vault and gc_failed_entries both warned 'missing field id' and skipped the co-located rotation-high-water.json floor sidecar on every scan; harmless (GC never deletes .json, only .bin) but noisy — fixed by skipping known floor-sidecar filenames before parse attempts via is_reserved_floor_sidecar

Added a bounded (5s) mount-init authoritative sent_shares refresh plus a 2s-interval background 'fuse-publish-pump' thread (using unique never-seen lookup names to defeat SMB negative-lookup caching) to drive the FUSE op that drains the otherwise edge-triggered publish queue on an idle macOS mount

workflow: When batching multiple independent code fixes destined for the same CI run, hold all pushes until every fix is ready, then push once — minimizes real-mount/CI round-trip cost (each desktop-e2e run costs ~15-40 min across 3 platforms)

Delegate deep root-cause debugging to a dedicated debugger subagent with explicit instructions to prove/disprove hypotheses and NOT apply a fix without confirming real vs fixture bug first — prevents papering over genuine product bugs with test hacks
Resume (not respawn) a subagent that already holds full context of a live repro/investigation rather than spawning a fresh one — much cheaper for complex multi-step diagnoses

Use an adversarial reviewer subagent to independently verify each CodeRabbit/Greptile finding against real code before fixing — correctly refutes false positives (e.g. borrowed-not-copied key buffers that are never actually zeroed) while confirming real bugs

When a live E2E test run is required to close an SC/acceptance gate and can't run in the current sandbox, treat CI as the authoritative arbiter and defer local validation to targeted offline proof tests (e.g. FakeTransport publish-count assertions) instead
Always rebuild cross-package dists (sdk-core → sdk → api etc.) before running consumer test suites after changing a shared lower-level package, to avoid false failures from stale dist artifacts
Verify subagent-reported 'diagnostics'/'never used' warnings against an authoritative build tool before acting — mid-edit tool snapshots frequently misreport during concurrent editing

friction: Canary-first (single-plan) execution of Wave 1 was flagged by the user as not matching their explicit request for all 4 plans to run concurrently — required correcting to full concurrent dispatch
Simultaneous git worktree creation across concurrent plan dispatches risks a `.git/config.lock` race, requiring dispatches to be issued in separate messages rather than truly simultaneously
Plan 03's unscoped `cargo fmt --all` stranded out-of-scope drift across ~13 unrelated files, blocking cleanup-wave merge with worktree_dirty until manually discarded
Wave 3 post-merge gate showed 3 false test failures due to stale sdk-core dist not rebuilt after a Wave 2 sdk-core change — required rebuilding dists to get true green

Desktop-e2e Step 8 required multiple debugging cycles across 3 platforms: revocation-bypass bug, double-publish bug (fuser fixed, then discovered missing on WinFsp), and macOS-specific idle-mount publish-queue starvation — each surfaced only after a real CI round-trip (~15-40 min each)
Windows CI failed once with a transient STATUS_DLL_INIT_FAILED (0xC0000142) API-startup flake unrelated to code, requiring a job re-run

Two rust-analyzer processes consumed ~11GB RAM combined; one was an orphaned leftover from a deleted Phase-69 worktree checkout with a dangling parent Claude Code session, requiring manual discovery and cleanup

CodeRabbit CLI + PR-level review together surfaced 7+ findings requiring careful triage (fix vs refute vs defer), including one genuine ship-blocking security/data-loss bug (build_scope_exit_child_override fail-open) not initially caught by the phase's own verification/security audit

Committing large files (engine.ts) through slow eslint/lint-staged pre-commit hooks repeatedly hit the 120-300s Bash timeout mid-commit, requiring status checks to confirm partial success before continuing

Local `cargo fmt -p cipherbox-fuse` produced different formatting output than what was already committed and CI-passing (rustfmt version skew), requiring reverting unnecessary fmt churn since CI doesn't fmt-check at all
First-ever PR CI run on a 96-commit no-PR branch surfaced two previously-hidden gate failures (SC#6 grep marker adjacency, Windows winfsp cfg gate) that had never been exercised until the PR opened
